hook: "YOUR CPM SHOULD NOT REQUIRE A PRESCRIPTION." — pharma-ad parody headline.
body: Full pharma-spoof script: "If your brand is suffering from Chronic High CPM, low views, weak distribution and sudden unexplained drops in attention… ask your marketer if @clipur is right for you (be aware there may be side effects). Clipur may help relieve: → paying $20+ CPMs for mediocre reach → content dying after one post → 'boost it again' syndrome → chronic dependence on paid ads. PLEASE do not use Clipur if you enjoy lighting your ad budget on fire. *Side effects may include lower CPMs, creator-led distribution, more organic eyeballs and becoming extremely irritated by what you used to pay for attention."
cta: "Full livestream is up. GO run it back and let me know the most clippable moments!" (engagement CTA, not a purchase CTA).
idea: A pharmaceutical-ad parody where the "condition" is high CPMs, the "drug" is @clipur, and the listed side effects are all benefits — the format's textbook execution.
sequencing: The parody headline (CPM shouldn't require a prescription)
The prescription ("ask your marketer if @clipur is right for you")
The relief list (4 marketer pain points)
The contraindication joke (don't use if you enjoy burning budget)
The fine-print flip (side effects = lower CPMs, organic eyeballs, irritation at old prices)
formatting: Text post + 57s video; pharma-spoof script written for video VO.
why_it_works: The pharma-ad grammar (diagnosis → prescription → side-effect fine print) is instantly recognizable, so the parody lands in seconds — and flipping the fine print into benefits makes the joke do the selling.
what_to_steal: LC's version: "WARNING: side effects of wearing waterproof jewelry may include compliments from strangers, never taking it off, and friends asking where it's from" — pharma-label static or 10s VO.
